# custom-handlers

Beyond CRUD — when your domain refuses to fit a table.

## README

# Custom handlers

Replace the default CRUD with handler bodies that carry business rules.
This recipe ships a `counter` entity with three custom write handlers
(create, increment with read-modify-write, reset with last-writer-wins)
plus a custom query that filters the projection.

The point is to show the **boundary**: where the entity executor stops
doing work for you and where your code has to take over. The framework
gives you `createEntityExecutor` so the executor's `create` / `update` /
`detail` / `list` are still one-liners — only the surrounding business
logic is yours.

## What it shows

- **`r.writeHandler({ name, schema, handler, access })`** — the inline
  form, useful when the handler body is short and stays close to its
  registration.
- **Read-modify-write with optimistic locking** — `increment` reads the
  current count, computes the new one, and updates with the version it
  read. Two concurrent increments cannot both succeed.
- **`createMany` for many rows in one handler** — `create-many` writes all
  events with one append statement and projects the rows in one savepoint;
  one invalid row fails the whole batch, nothing is written.
- **`skipOptimisticLock` for last-writer-wins** — `reset` deliberately
  bypasses the version check because the operation is admin-driven and
  resetting twice is semantically the same as resetting once.
- **Named verbs** — `verbs` on the entity and `update(..., { verb })` write
  `counter.archived` or `counter.reset` instead of `counter.updated`. The
  executor checks the declared transition (`archive` fails with
  `invalid_transition` unless the status is `open`) and sets the field.
- **`history` and `listAsOf`** — `history({ id })` returns the lifecycle and
  verb events of one counter, `listAsOf({ asOf })` folds the events up to an
  instant into rows.
- **Custom queries** — `counter:active` passes a server-side `filter`
  (`eq`/`ne`/`lt`/`gt`/`lte`/`gte`/`in`) and `totalCount` to the executor's
  list. Never filter a page in TypeScript: list is paginated, so rows after
  the first page would be missed.
- **`failNotFound` helper** — typed error response for the 404 case
  without a hand-built `KumikoError` subclass.

## When to reach for it

You have an entity but the default CRUD doesn't capture what your
business rule actually does. The default `update` blindly writes the
payload; your `increment` needs to read first, decide, and write. That's
the line.

## Source

The whole feature lives in `src/feature.ts` (~100 lines). Integration
tests cover the optimistic-lock case, the skip-lock case, and the
custom-filter query.

```bash
bun kumiko test integration samples/custom-handlers
```

// Custom Handlers Sample — Integration Test
// Proves: custom business logic in handlers, payload transformation, custom queries

import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import type { SaveContext } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine";
import { createTestUser, TestUsers, testTenantId } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/seeding";
import { expectErrorIncludes } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers";
import { setupTestStack, type TestStack } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/stack";
import { counterFeature } from "../feature";

let stack: TestStack;

const admin = TestUsers.admin;
const user = createTestUser({ id: 2, roles: ["User"] });

beforeAll(async () => {
  stack = await setupTestStack({ features: [counterFeature] });
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await stack.cleanup();
});

beforeEach(() => {
  stack.events.reset();
});

describe("custom write handler: increment", () => {
  test("increment adds to existing count", async () => {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      {
        name: "page-views",
      },
      admin,
    );
    expect(created.data["count"]).toBe(0);

    const incremented = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: created.id,
        amount: 5,
      },
      user,
    );

    expect(incremented.data["count"]).toBe(5);
    expect(incremented.data["lastIncrementedBy"]).toBe(`user:${user.id}`);
  });

  test("multiple increments accumulate", async () => {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      {
        name: "clicks",
      },
      admin,
    );

    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: created.id,
        amount: 3,
      },
      user,
    );
    const result = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: created.id,
        amount: 7,
      },
      user,
    );

    expect(result.data["count"]).toBe(10);
  });

  test("increment validates max amount", async () => {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      {
        name: "guarded",
      },
      admin,
    );

    const error = await stack.http.writeErr(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: created.id,
        amount: 101,
      },
      user,
    );
    expectErrorIncludes(error, "validation");
  });

  test("increment on non-existent returns error", async () => {
    const error = await stack.http.writeErr(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000999",
        amount: 1,
      },
      user,
    );
    expect(error.code).toBe("not_found");
  });
});

describe("custom write handler: create-many", () => {
  test("creates every row with count 0", async () => {
    const { ids } = await stack.http.writeOk<{ ids: string[] }>(
      "counters:write:counter:create-many",
      { names: ["batch-a", "batch-b", "batch-c"] },
      admin,
    );
    expect(ids).toHaveLength(3);

    const names: unknown[] = [];
    for (const id of ids) {
      const row = await stack.http.queryOk<Record<string, unknown>>(
        "counters:query:counter:detail",
        { id },
        admin,
      );
      expect(row["count"]).toBe(0);
      names.push(row["name"]);
    }
    expect(names).toEqual(["batch-a", "batch-b", "batch-c"]);
  });

  test("an invalid name fails the whole batch and writes no row", async () => {
    const error = await stack.http.writeErr(
      "counters:write:counter:create-many",
      { names: ["ok", ""] },
      admin,
    );
    expectErrorIncludes(error, "validation");

    const active = await stack.http.queryOk<{ rows: Record<string, unknown>[] }>(
      "counters:query:counter:active",
      { minCount: 0 },
      admin,
    );
    expect(active.rows.map((row) => row["name"])).not.toContain("ok");
  });
});

describe("custom write handler: reset", () => {
  test("reset sets count back to zero", async () => {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      {
        name: "resettable",
      },
      admin,
    );

    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      {
        id: created.id,
        amount: 42,
      },
      user,
    );

    const reset = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:reset",
      {
        id: created.id,
      },
      admin,
    );

    expect(reset.data["count"]).toBe(0);
    expect(reset.data["lastIncrementedBy"]).toBe("");
  });

  test("only Admin can reset", async () => {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      {
        name: "admin-only-reset",
      },
      admin,
    );

    const error = await stack.http.writeErr(
      "counters:write:counter:reset",
      {
        id: created.id,
      },
      user,
    );
    expect(error.code).toBe("access_denied");
  });
});

describe("custom query handler: active counters", () => {
  // Own tenants: the total assertions would otherwise count counters created by other tests.
  const activeAdmin = createTestUser({ roles: ["Admin"], tenantId: testTenantId(11) });
  const activeUser = createTestUser({ id: 2, roles: ["User"], tenantId: testTenantId(11) });
  const otherAdmin = createTestUser({ roles: ["Admin"], tenantId: testTenantId(12) });

  test("filters counters by minimum count", async () => {
    const c1 = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      { name: "active-a" },
      activeAdmin,
    );
    const c2 = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      { name: "active-b" },
      activeAdmin,
    );
    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      { name: "inactive" },
      activeAdmin,
    );

    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      { id: c1.id, amount: 10 },
      activeUser,
    );
    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:increment",
      { id: c2.id, amount: 5 },
      activeUser,
    );

    const result = await stack.http.queryOk<{
      rows: Record<string, unknown>[];
      nextCursor: string | null;
      total?: number;
    }>("counters:query:counter:active", { minCount: 5 }, activeAdmin);

    const names = result.rows.map((r) => r["name"]);
    expect(names).toContain("active-a");
    expect(names).toContain("active-b");
    expect(names).not.toContain("inactive");
    expect(result.total).toBe(2);
  });

  test("total and nextCursor describe the full filtered set", async () => {
    for (const name of ["total-a", "total-b", "total-c"]) {
      const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
        "counters:write:counter:create",
        { name },
        otherAdmin,
      );
      await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
        "counters:write:counter:increment",
        { id: created.id, amount: 1 },
        otherAdmin,
      );
    }
    await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      { name: "total-untouched" },
      otherAdmin,
    );

    const result = await stack.http.queryOk<{
      rows: Record<string, unknown>[];
      nextCursor: string | null;
      total?: number;
    }>("counters:query:counter:active", { minCount: 1 }, otherAdmin);

    expect(result.rows).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(result.total).toBe(3);
    expect(result.nextCursor).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("named verbs and history", () => {
  type HistoryEntry = { verb: string; at: string };

  async function createCounter(name: string): Promise<string> {
    const created = await stack.http.writeOk<SaveContext>(
      "counters:write:counter:create",
      { name },
      admin,
    );
    return String(created.id);
  }

  function historyOf(id: string): Promise<HistoryEntry[] | null> {
    return stack.http.queryOk<HistoryEntry[] | null>(
      "counters:query:counter:history",
      { id },
      admin,
    );
  }

  test("history lists lifecycle and verb events in order", async () => {
    const id = await createCounter("verb-history");
    await stack.http.writeOk("counters:write:counter:increment", { id, amount: 1 }, admin);
    await stack.http.writeOk("counters:write:counter:archive", { id }, admin);

    expect((await historyOf(id))?.map((entry) => entry.verb)).toEqual([
      "created",
      "updated",
      "archived",
    ]);
  });

  test("archiving twice is an invalid transition", async () => {
    const id = await createCounter("archive-twice");
    await stack.http.writeOk("counters:write:counter:archive", { id }, admin);

    const error = await stack.http.writeErr("counters:write:counter:archive", { id }, admin);

    expectErrorIncludes(error, "invalid_transition");
  });

  test("reset writes the reset verb", async () => {
    const id = await createCounter("verb-reset");
    await stack.http.writeOk("counters:write:counter:reset", { id }, admin);

    expect((await historyOf(id))?.map((entry) => entry.verb)).toEqual(["created", "reset"]);
  });

  test("as-of the created event shows the counter as it was", async () => {
    const id = await createCounter("as-of");
    await stack.http.writeOk("counters:write:counter:increment", { id, amount: 7 }, admin);
    const createdAt = (await historyOf(id))?.find((entry) => entry.verb === "created")?.at;
    if (createdAt === undefined) throw new Error("expected a created entry");

    const rows = await stack.http.queryOk<Record<string, unknown>[]>(
      "counters:query:counter:as-of",
      { asOf: createdAt },
      admin,
    );

    const row = rows.find((candidate) => candidate["id"] === id);
    expect(row?.["count"]).toBe(0);
    expect(row?.["status"]).toBe("open");
  });
});

### src/feature.ts

```ts
// Custom Handlers Sample
// Shows: writeHandler with business logic, queryHandler with a server-side filter,
// handler that modifies payload before DB write, named entity verbs (counter.archived,
// counter.reset) with a checked transition, and the executor's history and as-of reads.

import {
  createEntity,
  createEntityExecutor,
  createNumberField,
  createSelectField,
  createTextField,
  defineFeature,
} from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine";
import { failNotFound } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/errors";
import { z } from "zod";

export const counterEntity = createEntity({
  name: "counter",
  table: "read_sample_counters",
  fields: {
    name: createTextField({ personal: false, reason: "is_business_data", required: true }),
    count: createNumberField({ default: 0 }),
    lastIncrementedBy: createTextField({ personal: "ref" }),
    status: createSelectField({ options: ["open", "archived"], default: "open" }),
  },
  verbs: {
    archived: { transition: { field: "status", from: ["open"], to: "archived" } },
    reset: {},
  },
});

export const counterFeature = defineFeature("counters", (r) => {
  r.entity(counterEntity);

  // createEntityExecutor bundles buildEntityTable + createEventStoreExecutor —
  // the same pair every custom write-handler opens with. Collapses 3 lines
  // + the { entityName } bookkeeping into one destructure.
  const { executor: counterExecutor } = createEntityExecutor(counterEntity);

  // Standard create
  r.writeHandler({
    name: "counter:create",
    schema: z.object({ name: z.string().min(1) }),
    handler: async (event, ctx) =>
      counterExecutor.create({ ...event.payload, count: 0 }, event.user, ctx.db),
    access: { roles: ["Admin"] },
  });

  // Many rows in one handler: one append statement for all events, all or nothing
  r.writeHandler({
    name: "counter:create-many",
    schema: z.object({ names: z.array(z.string().min(1)).min(1).max(100) }),
    handler: async (event, ctx) => {
      const result = await counterExecutor.createMany(
        event.payload.names.map((name) => ({ name, count: 0 })),
        event.user,
        ctx.db,
      );
      if (!result.isSuccess) return result;
      return { isSuccess: true, data: { ids: result.data.map((saved) => saved.id) } };
    },
    access: { roles: ["Admin"] },
  });

  // Custom handler: increment with business logic
  r.writeHandler({
    name: "counter:increment",
    schema: z.object({ id: z.uuid(), amount: z.number().min(1).max(100) }),
    handler: async (event, ctx) => {
      const current = await counterExecutor.detail({ id: event.payload.id }, event.user, ctx.db);
      if (!current) {
        return failNotFound("counter", event.payload.id);
      }

      // detail() returns the entity's own row type; count is nullable because the field is not required.
      const { count, version } = current;
      const newCount = (count ?? 0) + event.payload.amount;
      // Read-modify-write on counter: use the version we just read so two
      // concurrent increments don't clobber each other's changes.
      return counterExecutor.update(
        {
          id: event.payload.id,
          version,
          changes: { count: newCount, lastIncrementedBy: `user:${event.user.id}` },
        },
        event.user,
        ctx.db,
      );
    },
    access: { roles: ["Admin", "User"] },
  });

  // Custom handler: reset to zero
  r.writeHandler({
    name: "counter:reset",
    schema: z.object({ id: z.uuid() }),
    handler: async (event, ctx) =>
      // Admin reset: last-writer-wins is intentional — there's no useful
      // concurrent-reset race to guard against.
      counterExecutor.update(
        { id: event.payload.id, changes: { count: 0, lastIncrementedBy: "" } },
        event.user,
        ctx.db,
        { skipOptimisticLock: true, verb: "reset" },
      ),
    access: { roles: ["Admin"] },
  });

  r.writeHandler({
    name: "counter:archive",
    schema: z.object({ id: z.uuid() }),
    handler: async (event, ctx) =>
      // The executor checks the transition and sets status.
      counterExecutor.update({ id: event.payload.id, changes: {} }, event.user, ctx.db, {
        skipOptimisticLock: true,
        verb: "archived",
      }),
    access: { roles: ["Admin"] },
  });

  // Custom query: only counters above a threshold. list() returns one page
  // (default 50, max 200, MAX_LIST_LIMIT), so a JS filter would miss rows after
  // page 1; filter in the query instead. totalCount counts over the whole WHERE.
  r.queryHandler({
    name: "counter:active",
    schema: z.object({ minCount: z.number().int().default(1), cursor: z.string().optional() }),
    handler: async (query, ctx) =>
      counterExecutor.list(
        {
          filter: { field: "count", op: "gte", value: query.payload.minCount },
          totalCount: true,
          cursor: query.payload.cursor,
        },
        query.user,
        ctx.db,
      ),
    access: {
      openToAll: {
        reason:
          "any signed-in user may list active counters; the sample has no per-user counter ownership",
      },
    },
  });

  // Standard detail
  r.queryHandler({
    name: "counter:detail",
    schema: z.object({ id: z.uuid() }),
    handler: async (query, ctx) => counterExecutor.detail(query.payload, query.user, ctx.db),
    access: {
      openToAll: {
        reason:
          "any signed-in user may read a counter by id; the sample has no per-user counter ownership",
      },
    },
  });

  r.queryHandler({
    name: "counter:history",
    schema: z.object({ id: z.uuid() }),
    handler: async (query, ctx) =>
      counterExecutor.history({ id: query.payload.id }, query.user, ctx.db),
    access: {
      openToAll: {
        reason:
          "any signed-in user may read a counter's history; the sample has no per-user counter ownership",
      },
    },
  });

  r.queryHandler({
    name: "counter:as-of",
    schema: z.object({ asOf: z.iso.datetime() }),
    handler: async (query, ctx) =>
      counterExecutor.listAsOf(
        { asOf: Temporal.Instant.from(query.payload.asOf) },
        query.user,
        ctx.db,
      ),
    access: {
      openToAll: {
        reason:
          "any signed-in user may read counters as of a past instant; the sample has no per-user counter ownership",
      },
    },
  });
});
```
